title: Why copper(II) solutions are blue
caption: In [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ an electron is promoted from t₂g to eg by absorbing light near 800 nm (red and orange), about 150 kJ mol⁻¹. The light transmitted is the complementary colour, so the solution looks pale blue. Changing the ligand changes Δo and so the colour.
alt: Energy diagram: t₂g and eg levels with an upward arrow labelled absorbs about 800 nm, and a note that the complementary blue is transmitted.
description: Arrow up: a photon of about 800 nm absorbed, ΔE = hc/λ ≈ 150 kJ mol⁻¹.
